speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand the progression of your symptoms better to help you. Can you tell me if these memory lapses, weakness, and paranoid thoughts have been getting worse over time, and how long ago your first fall occurred?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning combination of rapidly developing cognitive decline and focal neurological deficits in a 44-year-old. Given the acute onset of leg weakness and gait instability alongside memory loss, I need to rule out structural causes like a tumor or demyelination. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System (PACNS).

The combination of rapidly progressive multifocal neurological deficits (right leg weakness, gait instability), subacute cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms in a young male is highly suggestive of a primary CNS vasculitis. The MRI and lumbar puncture results ordered previously should show multifocal white matter lesions and a lymphocytic pleocytosis with elevated protein.
